title: A module over a Noetherian ring embeds in the product of its localizations at its associated primes
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $M$ an $R$-module. Call a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ an associated prime of $M$ if $\mathfrak p=\{a\in R:az=0\}$ for some $z\in M$, and write $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ for the set of them. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ let $M_{\mathfrak p}$ be the localization of $M$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the $R$-linear map $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)}M_{\mathfrak p}$, $m\mapsto(m/1)_{\mathfrak p}$, is injective (the empty product being $0$). Equivalently: if $m\in M$ and for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ there is $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $sm=0$, then $m=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero), lines 15495-15515 (statement and proof); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 0311,algebra-lemma-zero-at-ass-zero

proof.text: Let $m\in M$ map to zero in every $M_{\mathfrak p}$ for $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$, and suppose $m\ne0$. The cyclic submodule $N=Rm\subseteq M$ is nonzero. Since $0\cdot m=0$, the scalar $0$ is a zerodivisor on $N$; by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], $0$ lies in some associated prime $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$. Thus $\operatorname{Ass}(N)$ is nonempty, as required in the first sentence of the source proof.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-submodule] for $N\subseteq M$, the prime $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$ chosen in Step 1 belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$. Hence the kernel assumption gives $m/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero), proof lines 15509-15512, citing Lemma Tag 02M3 (lemma-ass, line 15131)

proof.text: Because $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$, choose $z\in N$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$ and write $z=rm$ for some $r\in R$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $m/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$ means that some $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ satisfies $sm=0$. Then $sz=srm=0$, so $s\in\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$, a contradiction. Thus $m=0$; this includes the empty-product case, since a nonzero $m$ would have produced an associated prime in Step 1.

lean.statement: theorem injective_pi_localization_associatedPrimes (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Function.Injective (LinearMap.pi (fun p : associatedPrimes R M => (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.1.primeCompl M : M →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.1 M))) ∧ (∀ m : M, (∀ p : associatedPrimes R M, ∃ s : R, s ∉ p.1 ∧ s • m = 0) → m = 0)
